metadata.description: The foreman dev workflow (commands, skills, agents) plus a library of standalone, opt-in rule packs for omp

plugins.name: foreman
plugins.description: GitHub-issue-tracker-driven dev workflow — ideas -> epics/tasks -> worktrees -> stacked PRs -> operator merge — as reusable commands (invoked as /foreman:<name>), skills, and agents. Config-driven via .omp/foreman.json; no hardcoded repo or toolchain.

plugins.name: craft
plugins.description: Ten model-invoked reference skills for the thinking around a change: grilling a decision to settle it, domain modeling (CONTEXT.md + ADRs), deep-module design vocabulary, what makes a test worth keeping, two-axis code review, the hard-bug diagnosis loop, prototyping, primary-source research, merge-conflict resolution, and writing documents agents consume. Adapted from mattpocock/skills (MIT).

plugins.name: git-hygiene
plugins.description: Guards for irreversible git operations and for the default branch: destructive commands (reset --hard, clean -fd, branch -D, stash drop), bare --force pushes, direct pushes and local merges to main, and a standing rule that the default branch is read-only. Workflow-agnostic.

plugins.name: verification-integrity
plugins.description: Guards against faking a green build: narrowing the test suite (.only/.skip, retries, blind snapshot updates) and bypassing git hooks with --no-verify. Workflow-agnostic.

plugins.name: generated-files
plugins.description: Stops hand-edits to machine-generated artifacts: *.generated.*, __generated__/, protobuf stubs, GraphQL schemas, ORM migrations, and OpenAPI clients. Edit the source and re-run the generator. Excludes package-manager lockfiles — those live in the per-manager packs.

plugins.name: shell-safety
plugins.description: Guards for irreversible or over-privileged shell operations: rm -rf, sudo, world-writable chmod, curl | sh, and truncating > redirects into source files. Complements git-hygiene, which owns the git-specific commands.

plugins.name: secrets-hygiene
plugins.description: Keeps credentials out of the repo and out of transcripts: writing .env and key files, staging them, dumping an environment, and inline passwords in shell commands.

plugins.name: pnpm
plugins.description: For repos whose package manager is pnpm: blocks npm/yarn/bun/npx invocations, hand-edited pnpm-lock.yaml, --no-frozen-lockfile, and unscoped workspace-root installs.

plugins.name: npm
plugins.description: For repos whose package manager is npm: blocks pnpm/yarn/bun invocations, hand-edited package-lock.json, npm install where npm ci belongs, and --legacy-peer-deps/--force escape hatches.

plugins.name: yarn
plugins.description: For repos whose package manager is yarn (Classic and Berry): blocks npm/pnpm/bun invocations, hand-edited yarn.lock, mutable installs (--no-immutable/--pure-lockfile), and --ignore-engines/--ignore-integrity.

plugins.name: bun
plugins.description: For repos whose package manager is bun: blocks npm/pnpm/yarn/npx invocations, hand-edited bun.lock and bun.lockb (binary), and --force/--no-save installs.

plugins.name: uv
plugins.description: For Python repos managed by uv: blocks pip/poetry/pipenv/conda installs that bypass uv.lock, hand-edited uv.lock, --system/--break-system-packages, and bare python where uv run belongs.

plugins.name: pip
plugins.description: For Python repos using pip and virtualenv directly: blocks installs outside a venv (sudo pip, --user, --break-system-packages), unpinned ad-hoc installs, hand-edited pip-compile output, and --no-deps/--force-reinstall.

plugins.name: cargo
plugins.description: For Rust repos: blocks hand-edited Cargo.lock, blanket cargo update, command-line clippy suppression (--cap-lints allow, -A clippy::all), and cargo publish without a dry run.
